site.title: Taiwan Internet History Hub
site.tagline: Explore Taiwan’s digital evolution — from TANet and dial-up, through broadband, to today’s 5G and satellite-ready society.

stages.title: Stage I — Academic Foundations & Dial-Up (1980s–Mid-1990s)
stages.summary: Taiwan plugs into the global Internet through academia, then opens dial-up to the public. Small user base, big implications.
technical: Dec 3, 1991: 64 Kbps international link via JvNCnet (first global connection).
1992–1994: SEEDNet trials; Chunghwa’s HiNet public dial-up.
Dial-up speeds 14.4–56 kbps; urban-heavy; metered costs.
societal: Users: academics, tech pros, urban early adopters.
1993: Early BBS-driven student protest (NCTU cafeteria case).
1996: “Telecom Three Laws” liberalize market, ending monopoly.
stages.context: TANet set TCP/IP norms early; BBS culture seeded civic participation that scaled later.

stages.title: Stage II — Broadband Rollout & Expansion (Late 1990s–2000s)
stages.summary: From dial-up to always-on: ADSL and fiber push Taiwan into the broadband age.
technical: Mid-2000s: FTTB/FTTH in cities; WiMAX trials (2009).
societal: Mass adoption: portals (Yahoo!奇摩), IM, online gaming, banking.
Gov’t: National Broadband Initiative, e-Taiwan (e-gov, inclusion).
PTT/blogs shape public discourse; early cyber-activism.
stages.context: Inclusion programs extended ADSL/fiber to rural and island communities, narrowing the access divide.

stages.title: Stage III — Mobile Internet & Social Media (2010s)
stages.summary: 4G + smartphones + social platforms transform daily life and politics.
technical: Median mobile speeds among world’s fastest by late-2010s.
2011: iTaiwan public Wi-Fi; city Wi-Fi (Taipei Free).
Dense fiber backhaul + ~14 subsea cables boost capacity.
societal: 2014: Sunflower Movement mobilized via PTT/social/live streams.
DIGI+ (2017–2025) funds gigabit goals & rural inclusion.
Open internet preserved; disinfo countered via fact-checking, not blocks.
stages.context: The 2010s cement the internet as Taiwan’s primary public square; civic tech and open government take root.

stages.title: Stage IV — 5G Era & Modern Digital Society (2020s–Present)
stages.summary: Near-ubiquitous connectivity, resilience planning, and digital governance.
technical: By mid-2020s: multi-million 5G subs; ~80+ Mbps median mobile.
LEO pilots; 6G & domestic satellite roadmap toward 2030.
societal: COVID tools: mask maps, SMS tracing; remote work/learn.
High internet freedom; Anti-Infiltration Act targets foreign interference.
2022: Ministry of Digital Affairs formed; cybersecurity prioritized.
stages.context: Focus shifts to resilience (redundant backbones, satellites), open-yet-secure info space, and scaling AI/IoT on 5G.

milestones: Academia online; Taiwan joins global Internet
